articles.summary: Jean Silva seeks Noche UFC glory
articles.body:
Jean Silva seeks Noche UFC redemption Saturday.

One year ago, Silva's night ended in disappointment as he was knocked out by Diego Lopes to close out the Mexican Independence Day event, a result that Lopes parlayed into a title fight with Alexander Volkanovski. Tonight, Silva takes on Jose Miguel Delgado in a headlining bout with considerably lower stakes.

Don't blame Delgado. The featherweight prospect jumped on the opportunity to replace an injured Yair Rodriguez and can now shake up the contender picture if he beats Silva. Delgado might not be a household name yet, but in the Year of the Upset, this roll of the dice could pay off in a big way for him.

What this win means for Silva is less clear, but don't expect the Brazilian fan favorite to be too bothered by the opponent switch. Whether it's against Delgado or Rodriguez or anyone else, Silva can always be relied upon to provide at least one memorable moment in his never-ending quest for glory—and bonus money.

Where: Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz.

When: Saturday, Sept. 12. The seven-fight preliminary card begins at 2 p.m. ET on Paramount+, followed by a six-fight main card at 5 p.m. ET also on Paramount+.

(Numbers in parentheses indicate standing in the MMA Fighting Global Rankings and MMA Fighting Pound-for-Pound Rankings )

Jose Miguel Delgado has all the tools to be a player at 145 pounds, but Jean Silva is too tall a task for him at this stage of his career. No pun intended.

Standing nearly six feet, Delgado presents a unique puzzle to anyone in the featherweight division, especially the relatively diminutive Silva. However, with a little over a dozen pro bouts to his name, he's a work in progress and like many young fighters, Delgado is still working on getting the most out of his tools and on the finer points of defense. Simply put, he hasn't faced a hitter like Silva yet.

I fully expect Delgado to give Silva all kinds of headaches early on, but with five rounds to work, Silva will figure him out and once he starts landing, Delgado's reactions will tell us everything we need to know about how his development is going. An upset wouldn't surprise me, but I like Silva to score a knockout to wash the bitter taste of last year's Noche UFC from his mouth.

A guy who couldn't make it out of the round of 16 on The Ultimate Fighter vs. the champion of Season 33? Mismatch!

While Moreno fell flat in his season of TUF (getting eliminated by some chump named Alexandre Pantoja), Morales valiantly clawed his way past Alibi Idris, Imanol Rodriguez, and Eduardo Chapolin to earn a well-deserved second UFC contract. Now, "Bopo" is the third up-and-coming flyweight in a row looking to bounce Moreno further down the rankings. What chance does Moreno have in the face of such adversity?

Jokes aside, a pretty good one. With respect to Morales, he's not Lone'er Kavanagh nor Tatsuro Taira. He's an excellent grappler and his high-level experience gives him a shot, but the standup is where he'll fall short against the two-time flyweight champion. Both Kavanagh and Taira proved to be major threats on the feet and that's an avenue Morales is yet to distinguish himself in.

Moreno gets back in the win column in an entertaining three-round striking affair that shows he still has some juice left in the tank.

I couldn't love this matchmaking more. Take two undefeated dudes and let The MMA Gods sort 'em out!

Tommy McMillen might be a future star in the eyes of the UFC, but he's been given decent competition without being put in situations that are over his head. Marwan Rahiki is a fine prospect in his own right and stands to gain a lot here if he can derail the McMillen hype train.

I'm comfortable picking McMillen just based on what we've seen recently from Rahiki. He can take a hit and bounce back, which is always a good sign, but if McMillen hurts him, he's not going to give Rahiki much room to breathe. As much polish as McMillen's striking still needs, he has a knack for volume you can't teach and that goes a long way towards separating him from the mid-tier of the stacked featherweight division.

McMillen will be put to the test here, because Rahiki has serious power and he's going to come out firing. I look forward to these two heading into deep waters, and McMillen just outlasting his fellow prospect for a late finish.

Manon Fiorot (2, P4P-5) vs. Alexa Grasso (5, P4P-10)

Yeah, I said it: Manon Fiorot and Alexa Grasso should be fighting for the vacant flyweight title in the main event of UFC 332.

I'm a big Natalia Silva fan and I'm happy she's getting her shot, especially considering she has a recent win over Grasso, but if I had to pick between these two matchups to headline a numbered event, it would be Fiorot vs. Grasso. I'll hear it the argument that they could have done Fiorot vs. Silva and instead had Grasso fight Wang Cong at Noche UFC, but I still think Fiorot vs. Grasso is the best fight of all the permutations.

We know Fiorot and Grasso can bang, and this is definitely a contrast of styles on the feet with Fiorot arguably having more pop in her punches, while Grasso is more of a volume and combination striker (though Maycee Barber can attest to Grasso having no shortage of KO power). Fans should prepare themselves for a technical battle as opposed to a slug-it-out war.

I'm curious to see how much grappling factors into this matchup. Fiorot knows her way around a takedown, but Grasso has wicked instincts on the mat whether it's attacking with a choke or laying in ground-and-pound. One stretch of sustained ground offense could make a huge difference on the cards.

This is way too close to call and I'm surprised that Fiorot is hovering around a healthy -250 as the favorite. I'm leaning towards Grasso to snag the upset via a stressfully close—and possibly contentious—decision.

Waldo Cortes-Acosta (7) vs. Curtis Blaydes (8)

What do we even make of the current state of Curtis Blaydes?

His brawl with Josh Hokit was ridiculously fun and showed a side of Blaydes we'd never seen before. On the other hand, in my eyes, that's the kind of fight that diminishes an athlete and it wouldn't surprise me if his chin isn't the same going forward. Heck, Blaydes has already been on the receiving end of some brutal knockouts, so I'm not sure there's much durability left.

That's why I've got to go with Waldo Cortes-Acosta here. He's not the athlete Hokit is, but I expect him to be able to handle the worst of Blaydes' grappling when this becomes a wrestling match. He's also a better puncher than Hokit, so anyone expecting Blaydes to take part in another brawl will be disappointed as a flurry from "Salsa Boy" should put him out.

That's how I see this fight ending, with Blaydes having early success before he leaves that chin hanging and pays the price for it.

David Martinez gets in there and takes care of business, and that's all he has to do to get past Dan Ige on Saturday.

This is Martinez's fight to lose, with Ige dropping down to 135 pounds in an effort to prolong what has been a solid UFC career. Ige was finished for the first time by Melquizael Costa and took that as a sign that his days as a featherweight were over. I'm not sure moving down to a division with faster fighters who still hit plenty hard is the solution to his woes, but I haven't fought over 20 times in the UFC, so what do I know?

Ige has shown flashes of explosive offense in his day, but he's going to have a difficult time getting a bead on Martinez, who fights safe and smart and, frankly, knows how to win. If he can find his finishing touch against Ige, that would raise him up another level in my eyes, but for now Martinez is doing just fine staying the course.

articles.title: Justin Gaethje Blames Arman Tsarukyan for His Title Woes, Still Backs Him to Win at UFC 331
articles.summary: Justin Gaethje weighs in on the potential #1 contender's bout between Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331.
articles.body:
The lightweight title picture is red hot after Justin Gaethje brutally stopped Ilia Topuria at UFC Freedom 250. While the Spaniard's team has already targeted an immediate rematch with Gaethje for his return, the American has firmly shut down that possibility. Instead, he is keeping a close eye on the upcoming UFC 331 co-main event between Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy.

Gaethje has made it clear in recent months that he sees Tsarukyan as the rightful No. 1 contender for the lightweight gold. However, the Armenian will first have to get past Ruffy when the two meet in Los Angeles on September 19. While many fans believe Tsarukyan should have fought for the title a long time ago, Dana White has had his reservations about the lightweight contender.

Those concerns largely stem from Tsarukyan pulling out just two days before UFC 311, where he was scheduled to challenge Islam Makhachev for the 155-pound title. Tsarukyan cited a back injury as the reason for his withdrawal. Since then, he has competed just once, at UFC Qatar in November 2025, making that his only fight in the past 27 months.

That, along with incidents such as his backstage brawls, is part of the reason Gaethje believes Tsarukyan has fallen out of the title picture. More importantly, Gaethje never bought the injury explanation behind his UFC 311 withdrawal. Speaking to Demetrious Johnson , he said, "We all make our own bed. He was going to fight Islam Makhachev for the belt. The truth is he wasn't going to make weight, so he dropped out."

He added, "If it was his back and there was a medical report on paper with the UFC, then he wouldn't be suffering like this. There's no way if he was truly to hurt his back cutting weight, how do you do that for one? Maybe his body was shutting down, and he just couldn't make weight, which happens."

Despite his doubts about Tsarukyan, Gaethje is still excited to see how he performs against Ruffy at UFC 331. However, he believes the Armenian could have a relatively easy night if he fights to his strengths.

He said, "As a fan, and even as an athlete that might fight these guys, I'm excited. I think Ruffy is on a tear right now, and his last two fights were ultimately super impressive, and I'm a huge fan of Bobby Green, but he fought Bobby Green and Michael Chandler, who aren't top three in the UFC. So, who has he fought who's in the top 10?"

Tsarukyan, meanwhile, has long been viewed as one of the division's top contenders. He defeated Charles Oliveira at UFC 300 and was also once viewed as a serious threat to an undefeated Ilia Topuria.

Gaethje added, "But this will be his first ultimate test in the UFC vs. a world-class fighter. I think Arman is world-class. Two very different stylistic matchups. Styles make matchups, and I don't know what we're going to see."

While Gaethje respects Tsarukyan's abilities, he is clearly hoping for a little chaos when the two lightweights finally collide. He said, "Most likely, Arman's going to take him down. I hope Arman gets hit hard. It would be fun to see. I don't hate Arman. I'd rather him get hit hard than see him get on top of him (Ruffy) and win. If he knocks out Ruffy, I'd be so happy."

Gaethje has already confirmed that he will not fight again in 2026 after securing twin title victories at UFC 324 and the White House event in June. For now, the lightweight champion can sit back and watch the contenders battle it out. It will be interesting to see who ultimately earns the chance to challenge Gaethje for the belt when he returns.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia Defeats Conor Benn via TKO, Punch Stats and Prize Money
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia continued his reign on Saturday night with a second-round TKO win over Conor Benn to retain his WBC welterweight title from T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia continued his reign on Saturday night with a second-round TKO win over Conor Benn to retain his WBC welterweight title from T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

The intensity was real from the opening bell in this one. Benn didn't hesitate to bring the fight to Garcia in the opening round, but King Ry was more than happy to fire back with his signature left hook.

That aggression turned out to be a bad choice for Benn in the second frame. Garcia connected with a right hand that floored Benn.

The Brit was able to work his way back to his feet, but the damage was done. Garcia swarmed him until the referee saw enough and waved off the fight.

The win gives Garcia his first successful world title defense just seven months after beating Mario Barrios for the belt.

The good news for Garcia is that there are several other big money fights to make within his division. Now that he's beaten Benn, he feels there are multiple big names that make sense and could generate a big payday.

I want Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. I have a lot of options. I'm not really worried about Haney now. If it happens, it happens," he told Manouk Akopyan of Ring Magazine.

"All these guys obviously have to come to me, you know what I mean? I'm definitely the lottery fight. If you want to be a huge name, I'm the guy to do it [against]. You have to get through me."

Only one of those opponents actually has another title for Garcia to collect. Teofimo Lopez holds the WBA title, although Jack Catterall is currently the "regular" WBA titleholder.

Still, Garcia could look to set up a rematch with Romero after losing to him via unanimous decision in May 2025.

The Guardian reported that both combatants are believed to have taken home around $15 million for their efforts.

It's safe to say that Garcia has even bigger paydays coming down the pike with this result.

articles.title: Conor Benn's Rival Slams Him On X After Highlight-Reel TKO Loss
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia's highlight-reel KO of Conor Benn sent shockwaves through the boxing world on Saturday night. Here's how some of the biggest fighters in the worl...
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia destroyed Conor Benn with a right hand from hell on Saturday night at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Garcia and Benn traded mean-spirited barbs throughout the build, but it was the WBC welterweight champion who made good on his promise to finish the British slugger inside five rounds. The end came in the second frame and it only took seconds for Benn's rival and others to take to social media with their reactions. Let's talk boxing.

Garcia's fastest stoppage since a first-round knockout of Francisco Fonseca in February 2020

The finish is not without argument. Benn was dropped by a clean right hand and then trapped along the ropes, and multiple live blogs flagged the referee's intervention as early, with Benn slipping shots at the moment Taylor stepped in. I initially thought it was a quick stoppage, but when I saw that Benn wasn't protesting the ref's call, I figured he was done. That's an underrated barometer of a referee's decision to stop a fight. If the fighter doesn't complain, that speaks louder than what others outside the ring may think.

Garcia called for unification fights with Teofimo Lopez and Devin Haney in his post-fight interview.

Chris Eubank Jr. and Benn have carried on the rivalry their fathers began decades ago. While Benn manhandled Eubank in the rematch and may have effectively retired him, the latter hasn't buried the hatchet. In fact, his post on X might be more like burying a hatchet in Benn's back.

Eubank has long spoken about how his weight cut for the fights with Benn affected his performance. Apparently, he believes that's what happened to Benn on Saturday.

Other fighters chimed in with their reactions. It seemed everyone from Claressa Shields to Danny Garcia, Sergio Mora, Jamel Herring and others all had takes on the result.

While many may have expected Garcia to win, it was tough to blow this one off as just another decent performance. The stoppage was electrifying.

Garcia did what he said he would do and he did it on the biggest stage. All of the sport's eyes were fixated on this event and it was a statement-making card for Zuffa Boxing. Jai Opetaia put on a strong performance in stopping Noel Mikaelian and Garcia topped it off with his destruction of Benn.

David Benavidez squared off with Opetaia after his win and Garcia called out Teofimo Lopez and Devin Haney — both were in attendance — for welterweight unification bouts.

All things considered, it couldn't have gone much better for Dana White and Co.

articles.body: Ryan Garcia made easy work of Conor Benn in his first title defense. Garcia stopped Benn in two rounds to retain his WBC welterweight title Saturday in front of a partisan crowd at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.In an electrifying Round 1, Benn came out fast against Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs), looking to close the gap and throw combinations. Garcia utilized his reach advantage and his fleet footwork to keep Benn at distance and walk him into left hands. Garcia knocked Benn (25-2, 14 KOs) off balance early in the contest with his trademark left hook, and his speed appeared to trouble Benn more than anything else. articles.title: 'Easiest money ever': Ryan Garcia's brutal destruction of Conor Benn sends fight world into a frenzy
articles.summary: The fight world reacts to Garcia's spectacular defense of his WBC welterweight title, including a sly remark from Benn's chief hater, Chris Eubank Jr.
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia left no doubt. After a heated build-up between two of boxing's biggest names, the reigning WBC welterweight champion delivered a devastating performance Saturday night inside of Las Vegas' T-Mobile Arena , needing less than two rounds to dispatch Conor Benn and successfully defend his belt in a statement performance.

After controlling the opening round, Garcia ended matters in spectacular fashion early in the second, uncorking a massive right hand that sent Benn crumbling to the canvas. Benn managed to beat the 10-count, but Garcia immediately swarmed his wounded prey and unloaded against the ropes until referee Thomas Taylor mercifully stopped the bout.

Afterward, Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) called for WBA welterweight champion Teofimo Lopez to join him in the ring, teasing the possibility of a massive unification clash next. Benn (25-2, 14 KOs), meanwhile, suffered the first stoppage loss of his pro career.

Unsurprisingly, as is often the case with anything Garcia does, Saturday's result instantly set the boxing world ablaze, prompting a flood of fellow fighters to gush over Garcia's spectacular performance on social media — and eliciting a healthy amount of revelry from Benn's critics. Chief among those critics was Chris Eubank Jr., who couldn't help but chime in with a roast of his longtime rival following their two-fight series in 2025.

"Welcome to the 'fighting after cutting too much weight' club… Enjoy"

articles.title: Silva somete a Delgado y se quita la espina clavada con el UFC Noche
articles.standfirst: El peleador brasileño sometió al mexicano para redimirse de su derrota de hace un año ante Diego Lopes
articles.summary: El peleador brasileño sometió al mexicano para redimirse de su derrota de hace un año ante Diego Lopes
articles.body: Hace un año, Jean Silva (18-3) vivió la cara amarga de la derrota en el UFC Noche al ser noqueado por Diego Lopes con un codazo giratorio. Sin embargo, en 2026 las cosas han cambiado para el peleador brasileño, ya que ha sometido a José Delgado (12-3) para echar por tierra sus aspiraciones en una noche muy especial para el pueblo mexicano. De esta forma, 'Lord' se queda a las puertas de una oportunidad por el título de peso pluma, aunque lo hizo sufriendo tras estar a punto de ser noqueado en el primer asalto. En teoría, Silva se debería haber enfrentado a Yair Rodriguez. Sin embargo, una lesión de 'El Pantera' obligó a la UFC a buscar un reemplazo en corto aviso, y fue Delgado el que se vio beneficiado al ser el otro gran nombre mexicano dentro de la división. Era un salto cualitativo muy grande para él, pero en el primer asalto conectó a Jean con buenas manos y estuvo muy cerca de lograr una de las mayores sorpresas del año. Lejos de venirse abajo, Silva pasó de ser calculador a ir al ataque, y tras una esquiva preciosa tumbó a Delgado con un golpe a la contra y le acabó sometiendo con un mataleón. Una actuación que puede que le valga para medirse por el cinturón de peso pluma al ganador del combate titular entre Alexander Volkanovski y Movsar Evloev que se disputará a finales de octubre en el UFC 333. En el combate co estelar México tuvo mejor suerte, ya que Brandon Moreno (24-10-2) logro superar a Joseph Morales (15-3) por decisión dividida para superar las dos derrotas consecutivas que había sumado en los últimos meses. El ex campeón de peso mosca se mostró muy técnico en el striking, y en la entrevista post victoria reconoció que estaba de vuelta tras haber pasado un bache a nivel emocional que había influido en sus actuaciones. Eso sí, el combate de la noche fue el que todo el mundo esperaba: Tommy McMillen (12-0) vs Marwan Rahiki (9-1). Mejor pelea del evento, y una de las mejores del año. Una guerra sin cuartel en la que el peleador australiano estuvo muy cerca de noquear al estadounidense en el segundo asalto, pero donde acabó sucumbiendo por decisión unánime ante el pundonor y la resiliencia del compañero de Sean O'Malley. De hecho, Tommy también pudo finalizar el pleito en el tercer round, pero ambos estaban demasiado cansados. Había mucho beef entre ambos antes de la pelea, y cumplieron con creces las expectativas en un duelo que posiblemente se repita dentro de unos años, cuando ambos estén asentados en el top 15 de peso pluma. Otra actuación destacable fue la de Alexa Grasso (18-5-1), que dio una clase en el striking a Manon Fiorot (13-3) para ganarse con creces una oportunidad por el cinturón de peso mosca femenino. Ahora que Valentina Shevchenko está lesionada de larga duración, lo normal es que sea la ex campeona de la categoría la que se mida a la ganadora del combate titular entre Natalia Silva y Wang Cong. Yousri Belgaroui (11-3) también brilló con luz propia con un brutal K.O. a Djorden Santos (11-4), al igual que Tommy Gantt (13-0, 1NC) con una gran sumisión a Drakkar Klose (16-4-1) en el tercer round. Sin embargo, la gran finalización de la cartelera la protagonizó Sean King III (7-0), con un súplex a Jessie Rosas (8-2) en apenas 30 segundos que silenció por completo al público de Arizona. Una Fight Night especial por lo que representa para México, y una velada que se puede catalogar como una de las mejores del año sin contar a las numeradas.
